skill.name: contribute-catalog
skill.description: Guide contributors through creating a HyperFrames registry block or component and preparing an upstream catalog pull request.
skill.summary: Create and submit HyperFrames catalog blocks or components.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static Ruby backtick detections are Markdown, JSON, or JavaScript template false positives rather than shell execution. Real risks remain around documented CLI execution, publishing, GitHub actions, AWS upload guidance, and third-party CDN resources. No evidence found for prompt injection or covert data-exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: Commands can publish, push, authenticate, or create pull requests.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running npx hyperframes publish, git push, gh auth login, or gh pr create.

remediation.issue: Internal image upload uses a named AWS profile.
remediation.suggestion: Limit the upload script to authorized maintainers, document required permissions, and avoid automatic execution by agents.

remediation.issue: npx commands may invoke package-managed tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer pinned local project dependencies and show the resolved command before execution.

remediation.issue: Generated templates load third-party CDN scripts and fonts.
remediation.suggestion: Consider vendoring approved assets or adding integrity controls for generated HTML templates.

content.value_statement: Creating a reusable HyperFrames catalog item requires structure, metadata, previews, and review steps. This skill guides contributors from idea to validated pull request.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies whether the contribution should be a block or a component.
Scaffolds the expected HyperFrames registry folder and metadata structure.
Provides starter templates for caption, VFX, and component contributions.
Defines animation, timing, naming, and preview requirements for catalog quality.
Lists validation, formatting, publishing, and pull request steps for maintainers.
limitations: Requires access to a HyperFrames repository checkout and compatible CLI tools.
Publishing, GitHub, and internal upload steps require user credentials and approval.
Starter templates must be customized for the requested visual style.
This skill is for public catalog contributions, not installing existing registry items.

use_cases.title: Submit a Caption Style
use_cases.description: Build a new caption block with readable text, timed word highlights, metadata, previews, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Create a VFX Block
use_cases.description: Prepare a Three.js-based visual effect with deterministic animation and catalog-ready preview assets.

use_cases.title: Review a Registry Addition
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed catalog item follows naming, metadata, validation, and publishing requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Catalog Idea
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner contributor planning a first item.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me contribute a HyperFrames catalog item. Ask what you need to know before choosing block or component.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a New Block
prompt_templates.scenario: Contributor has a clear visual concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the folder plan, metadata checklist, and implementation steps for a new HyperFrames block named [name].

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Contributor needs a working starter approach.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the appropriate HyperFrames contribution template for a [caption, VFX, or component] item and explain what I must replace.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Pull Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced contributor ready to submit upstream.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my catalog contribution plan and list the validation, preview, publish, and pull request steps I must complete.

output_examples.input: I want to add a bold karaoke caption style for social videos.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies this as a block, proposes a registry location, lists caption readability rules, and prepares validation and preview tasks.

output_examples.input: I built a shimmer overlay and want it in the public catalog.
output_examples.output: The skill classifies it as a component, checks naming and metadata needs, and describes how to package it for review.

output_examples.input: Before I open the pull request, check what I missed.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a submission checklist covering linting, validation, formatting, registry updates, generated docs, preview assets, and pull request details.

best_practices: Confirm the item type before creating files or metadata.
Run validation and preview steps before asking maintainers to review.
Ask before running commands that publish, push, authenticate, or upload assets.
anti_patterns: Using the contribution workflow for private in-project edits.
Submitting an item without preview media or generated catalog documentation.
Running publish, GitHub, or cloud upload commands without explicit user approval.

faq.question: Is this skill for using existing catalog items?
faq.answer: No. It is for contributing new public catalog blocks or components.

faq.question: What is the difference between a block and a component?
faq.answer: A block is a complete composition with dimensions and duration. A component is a reusable snippet inside another composition.

faq.question: Does it generate preview assets automatically?
faq.answer: It explains the preview workflow. The user still needs local tools and approval for publishing or uploads.

faq.question: Can it help with captions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes caption rules for readability, timing, karaoke highlights, and overflow handling.

faq.question: Can it help with Three.js effects?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides VFX guidance for deterministic rendering and timeline-controlled animation.

faq.question: Does it open the pull request for me?
faq.answer: It lists the pull request steps. Commands that push or create a pull request should require explicit confirmation.
